version.changelog: Initial release — full technical SEO audit + content brief generator

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: seo-audit-pro-rabie
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle provides a functional SEO audit tool, but the script `scripts/seo_audit.py` contains a security vulnerability by explicitly disabling SSL certificate verification (`ssl.CERT_NONE`) and hostname checking. While this is often done in simple scrapers to avoid certificate errors, it exposes the agent to potential man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks. Since the instructions in `SKILL.md` direct the agent to read the script's output fully, a MITM attacker could potentially inject malicious content into the audit report to influence the agent's behavior.

llm.summary: The skill is coherent with its stated purpose (it runs a local Python audit script that fetches pages and builds an SEO report), but it will perform arbitrary network requests and disables SSL verification — use in a controlled environment and avoid pointing it at sensitive internal endpoints.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the implementation: the SKILL.md tells the agent to run scripts/seo_audit.py which fetches the target URL, robots.txt, sitemap.xml and extracts on-page and technical signals. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or external services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions run a local script that makes network requests to any URL supplied by the user. The script will fetch arbitrary HTTP(S) endpoints (page, robots.txt, sitemap) and read their contents. This is expected for an audit tool but creates two concerns: (1) it can be used to probe internal IPs / private endpoints (SSRF-style probing) if given such URLs, and (2) the script disables SSL certificate verification (ctx.check_hostname = False; ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE), which weakens transport security and could mask MITM or invalid-certificate conditions. The SKILL.md does not warn about these behaviors.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; the skill is instruction-plus-script only. That is low-risk from an install perspective (nothing is downloaded/executed at install time). It assumes a Python 3 runtime is available but does not declare it explicitly.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, secrets, or config paths. The code does not attempt to read environment variables or other system credentials. Requested access is limited to network requests to the target URLs, which is proportionate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent/system-level privileges. There is no evidence it modifies other skills or agent-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement an SEO crawler/auditor and is internally consistent with that purpose. Before installing or running it: (1) be aware it will make arbitrary HTTP(S) requests to whatever URL you supply — do NOT point it at internal-only addresses (127.0.0.1, 10.*.*, 169.254.*, 192.168.* etc.) or other sensitive infrastructure unless you intentionally want that scanning; (2) the script disables SSL certificate verification, so results may accept invalid certs and mask TLS issues — consider enabling verification in the code if you need accurate security checks; (3) run it in an isolated or non-production environment if you are unsure (network-restricted container or VM); (4) review the rest of the script (the truncated portion) to confirm it doesn't send results to external endpoints — if the code subsequently posts data to unknown servers, that would change this assessment to suspicious. If you want higher assurance, request a full copy of scripts/seo_audit.py (complete file) and confirm there are no network callbacks or hidden upload endpoints.
